_about: Giten Megami Tensei script VM opcode table, recovered from dds_en.exe (dispatch table at VA 0x4318B0, 0x2FE entries).
_text_model: Bytes >= 0x20 are literal Shift-JIS text (2 bytes when the first is an SJIS lead byte). There is NO length field for text anywhere; a text run ends at the next control byte. 0x00 terminates a record fragment.

_escapes.0x1D: index 0x300 + next byte -- ALWAYS a 2-byte no-op (dispatcher rejects > 0x2FD)

_branches: rel16 operands are PC-RELATIVE: target = (offset_of_byte_after_the_rel16 + imm16) & 0xFFFF, measured inside the runtime buffer, which is [0x400-byte, 256-entry index][record data in id order]. Relocate a rel16 whenever the byte count between the end of the operand and its target changes.
_conditional_branch: Every conditional form is [rel16][condition operands] and branches when the condition evaluates to 0.

expressions._about: Operand slots of kind "expr" are recursive trees read by 0x436B00. First byte selects the node; the map below gives that node's ordered payload ("expr" = a nested tree). Node bytes above 0x5D are invalid.

0x101.note: print runtime string: [u8 selector] then [expr] (selectors 04-06,0C-0F,11,13) or [u8][expr] (all others); handler 0x436920, table 0x436A4C. Retyped 2026-09-04: the old u8-only model put span boundaries after a name print 3 bytes early (the 'Yuuka:' -> 'ka:' bug).

0x103.note: multi-condition branch (handler 0x0042FEB0): [rel16] then a list of 2-byte terms [u8 bank|0x80 negate][u8 index], terminated by an entry whose FIRST byte is 0xFF -- both bytes of that entry are consumed, because 0x004393E0 reads the pair before testing it.  1F03 ORs the terms, 1F04 ANDs them; both branch when the result is 0.  The old fixed rel16 + 4x u8 equals rel16 + two terms + terminator, so it was right for the 562 two-term sites and wrong for the 353 with three or more (38% of 915).  It never surfaced as a tiling failure because 0xFF >= 0x20, so the stranded bytes tokenised as one-byte text and the walk resynchronised.  Confirmed 2026-09-06 against engine traces: at all 15 sites where the tracer logged the next token PC after a 1F03/1F04, it equals terminator + 2; none equals terminator + 1 or start + 8.

0x14C.note: reads [u8][u8][expr] -- ONE expression, not two.  All six handlers 0x14C-0x151 push $1 and route through 0x004335E0, which is call 0x4335A0 (two READ_U8), then call 0x4335C0(arg), then call 0x437490 (one expression, unconditional).  0x004335C0 is 'cmpw $0x0,0x4(%esp) / jne 0x4335cd / jmp 0x437490' -- it reads an expression ONLY when its argument is 0, and every one of these opcodes passes 1, so it takes a global (0x481354) instead and consumes no stream bytes.  The old model read that second expression, over-consuming 3-6 bytes at each of 404 sites; it rarely surfaced as a tiling failure because the walk usually resynchronised.  Measured against the engine 2026-09-06: at 529 traced sites the engine consumed exactly 6 bytes where the model claimed 9-12.  Correcting it moved engine boundary agreement 93.33% -> 96.83% (30,802 traced token PCs), untiled records 111 -> 74, and records carrying an impossible expression selector 46 -> 43.

0x17F.note: handler 0x00430814 calls 0x00434740 with A=0.  That routine reads the rel16, then one expression, then a SECOND expression only when A==1 (cmp ecx,1 / jne).  A=0 means the comparison is against a literal zero, so this form takes rel16 + one expr; 0x185-0x189 pass A=1 and do take two.  B (0..5) picks the comparison through the six-entry jump table at 0x00434724.

_switch: 0E/0F operands are a 0xFF-terminated table: [u8 case][u8 kind][u16]; kind != 0 -> the u16 is a rel16 branch target (relocated), kind == 0 -> two bytes (file, record) naming another script file. Handler 0x4327C0, callers 0x4328C0 (0E, random) and 0x4328E0 (0F, menu selection byte at 0x4919E0).
_rtstr: 1F01 = format and print a runtime string; the selector picks the builder (07/08 = a character's name, 00 = the player's, ...). The string is executed as script from its own buffer (pc 0..) through a call frame, which is what the trace shows as pc=0 events.
